concerns.concern: The paper claims improved heat-to-electricity conversion but compares only effective conductivity with conventional devices. The composites' spin Seebeck coefficient is about 10–30× smaller than bulk Pt/YIG, so the power factor of conventional devices may actually be about an order of magnitude higher.
concerns.quote: A like-for-like PF comparison may therefore not favor the composites.

concerns.concern: There is no identically processed non-magnetic control composite, such as Pt-coated GGG or Al2O3. Without it, Pt-intrinsic or processing-related field-odd signals cannot be ruled out, so the claim that the signal is 'purely' SSE is stronger than the evidence supports.
concerns.quote: The most direct control would be an identically processed Pt-coated non-magnetic insulator composite, e.g., GGG or Al2O3 powder.

concerns.concern: The arguments against parasitic contributions are qualitative. XRD cannot detect minor or nm-thick interfacial phases, no Hall detection limit is given, and the paper admits α-Fe2O3/YFeO3 formation could not be distinguished. An overlay of E_y(H) with M(H) on the same piece is also requested.
concerns.quote: XRD typically cannot detect phases below ~1–5 wt%, or nm-thick interfacial phases at a Pt/YIG interface

concerns.concern: Getting the same coefficient in both geometries shows only isotropy. Any bulk transverse effect of the form E ∝ ∇T × M, including ANE from a minority ferromagnetic phase, would be isotropic in a random composite, so this does not specifically support SSE.
concerns.quote: The rotation test therefore establishes isotropy, not the SSE origin per se.

concerns.concern: The drop in magnetization after Pt deposition does not exclude a small ferromagnetic impurity fraction, because Pt dilution of the YIG moment could mask it. The argument needs a quantitative comparison with the expected Pt mass dilution.
concerns.quote: Pt simultaneously dilutes the YIG moment, so a net decrease does not exclude a small FM fraction.

concerns.concern: The '2–3 orders of magnitude' conductivity advantage is overstated. For the lower-conductivity samples the gain over the Pt/YIG single-crystal reference is only about 10–16×.
concerns.quote: The 15-RT sample (562 S/m) versus Pt(10 nm)/YIG single crystal (53 S/m) is only ~10×, one order of magnitude.

concerns.concern: The Pt-thickness dependence is explained with thin-film spin-diffusion-length intuition. However, effective conductivity rises 4–6× while the coefficient falls only ~20%, which a thin-film model does not predict and points instead to percolation/network effects.
concerns.quote: Invoking the thin-film thickness dependence as qualitative support is therefore misleading.

concerns.concern: Only one sample per condition was measured, all from a single batch. Sample-to-sample variability is therefore unknown, and trends attributed to processing (RT vs 300 °C pressing, Pt thickness, 630% PF variation) may not be reliable.
concerns.quote: Without repeats, it is unclear whether the differences reflect the processing variables.

concerns.concern: The rotated-geometry (Hx–∇zT) value, which underpins the isotropy claim, comes from a single temperature gradient. No check of linearity in ∇T is shown, so the ~3% agreement may be partly fortuitous.
concerns.quote: The rotated-geometry value comes from a single ∇zT = 2.64 K/mm (Fig. 3e), with no linear-in-∇T check

concerns.concern: The signal sign is not discussed. With E ∝ ∇T × M, the two geometries should give opposite signs for fixed conventions, yet both show positive E_y. Electrode polarity and ∇T sign conventions are not specified.
concerns.quote: Agreement in sign as well as magnitude would be a stronger consistency check.

concerns.concern: The 15- and 30-nm Pt thicknesses are nominal, extrapolated from deposition time rather than measured. On tumbling powders the actual thickness and coverage depend on surface area, batch mass and shadowing.
concerns.quote: the 15- and 30-nm thicknesses are not measured.

concerns.concern: Key fabrication and geometry parameters are missing: particle-size distribution, powder mass per sputtering run, pressing dwell time, and pellet and specimen dimensions. Without them the work is not reproducible, and the Pt fraction and the relation to the magnon length argument cannot be assessed.
concerns.quote: Without these, the work is not reproducible, the Pt volume fraction cannot be estimated

concerns.concern: In the Cu-block bridge geometry, the paper does not specify thermocouple locations, how the gradient is computed, or how drops at the thermal tape and contacts are handled. The authors themselves note that such interfacial drops bias S.
concerns.quote: The paper does not say where the thermocouples sit, how the in-plane gradient across the sample length is obtained, or how tape and contact drops are handled.

concerns.concern: The same PDF card number is assigned to both Y2O3 and FePt. Since the FePt reference lines are used to exclude a ferromagnetic metallic phase, the wrong card would undermine that exclusion.
concerns.quote: One assignment must be wrong.

concerns.concern: Fig. 3f appears to show similar saturation magnetization for the 15- and 30-nm samples, even though their Pt mass fractions should differ by about 2×. This is not discussed.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3f also appears to show similar Ms for the 15- and 30-nm samples, although the Pt mass fraction should differ by ~2×.

concerns.concern: The claim that composite conductivity exceeds that of oxide-based bulk ANE materials holds only for the 30-nm samples. The 15-nm samples fall within that range.
concerns.quote: so 'higher than' those materials holds only for the 30-nm samples.

concerns.concern: The effective conductivity of conventional devices depends mainly on the arbitrary substrate/ferromagnet thickness. This makes the conductivity comparison geometry-dependent.
concerns.quote: which makes the comparison somewhat geometry-dependent.

concerns.concern: The paper links being well above the spin diffusion length to the absence of Pt discontinuities. Continuity is actually set by the ~5 nm island-to-film threshold, and being far above λ_s reduces S through shunting.
concerns.quote: Continuity is governed by the island-to-film threshold (~5 nm, Fig. S2), not by λ_s.

concerns.concern: The origin of the lower spin Seebeck coefficient after 300 °C pressing is not discussed.
concerns.quote: The origin of the lower S after 300 °C pressing is also not discussed.

concerns.concern: The low thermal conductivity is attributed to interfacial phonon scattering. Constriction resistance at small particle–particle contacts in unsintered pressed powders is not considered, so the phonon-scattering explanation is speculative.
concerns.quote: Interfacial phonon scattering is therefore one of several possibilities and is speculative as stated.

concerns.concern: Relative density is computed against YIG density alone, ignoring the Pt contribution to the theoretical density. This overstates densification, especially for the 30-nm samples.
concerns.quote: The relative density is also computed against YIG alone (5.11 g/cm³), ignoring the Pt contribution to the theoretical density.

concerns.concern: The quoted YIG saturation magnetization (37.9 emu/g) is the zero-temperature value. The room-temperature value of ~27–28 emu/g should be used for comparison with the room-temperature measurements.
concerns.quote: 37.9 emu/g corresponds to 5 μ_B per Y3Fe5O12 formula unit, i.e., the T → 0 value.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3f axis shows the YIG crystal saturating near 0.027 'emu/g', three orders of magnitude below expected values. Either the units or the normalization is wrong, so the absolute magnetization comparisons cannot be verified.
concerns.quote: The y-axis is likely raw moment in emu, or the normalization is off.

concerns.concern: The isotropy comparison sentence names the wrong configuration and so compares the Hx–∇zT result with itself. It should refer to the Hz–∇xT configuration.
concerns.quote: As written, the sentence compares the measurement with itself

concerns.concern: Two different Cu-Kα wavelengths are used, 0.15406 nm in the Methods and 0.15418 nm in Note S2.
concerns.quote: the Methods use λ(Cu-Kα) = 0.15406 nm for the angle conversion while Note S2 states 0.15418 nm.

concerns.concern: Note S2 refers to the XRD data as Fig. S2, which is the TEM figure, instead of Fig. S3.
concerns.quote: Note S2 also refers to the XRD data as 'Fig. S2' (which is the TEM figure) rather than Fig. S3.

concerns.concern: The 'bad metal' label is inappropriate. The composites' conductivity is two to three orders below the Mott–Ioffe–Regel regime and is extrinsic, coming from a percolating network of good-metal Pt.
concerns.quote: The composites (σ ~ 10²–10³ S/m) are two to three orders below that.

concerns.concern: The abstract claims 'robust mechanical integrity' without any mechanical testing.
concerns.quote: the abstract's 'robust mechanical integrity' is asserted without any mechanical test
